perspective:
From Brandon Talayumptewa’s perspective, the information available to him is:

- I know my own identity and professional background: I am an insurance agent, Alaska Native, and have a bachelor’s degree. I experience myself as cautious and detail-oriented.
- I met Benjamin Erickson professionally for the first time when he sought business insurance advice. I understood him to be an entrepreneur. I was aware he had limited formal education, so I initially worried about explaining complex insurance terms clearly.
- In our first meeting, Benjamin told me he wanted comprehensive coverage and that some terms were new to him. I explained liability insurance as a safety net and gave the slip-and-fall example. I explained asset protection as covering inventory and equipment, like a guard over physical investments. Benjamin said this made sense, asked about assets, and thanked me for breaking it down.
- In a later meeting, I had revised my belief about Benjamin’s ability to understand detailed information and felt more confident. Benjamin said he was ready and had been reading up. I explained business interruption insurance and property insurance. Benjamin said that sounded crucial and reassuring.
- At a casual lunch, I felt insecure about how Benjamin perceived my cautious nature and tried to balance detail with engaging delivery. Benjamin said he appreciated my thoroughness but also enjoyed lighter moments. I told a joke about an entrepreneur insuring his taste buds for a million dollars. Benjamin was fascinated and said it made sense given the stakes. I related it to assessing unique risks for his business. Benjamin agreed it was less unusual but equally important.
- Pleased by Benjamin’s positive response to my personal anecdote, I decided to offer additional support beyond insurance. I asked whether he had considered strategic investments that could lower premiums. Benjamin said he hadn’t but liked the idea. I suggested upgraded security systems could protect assets and reduce insurance costs. Benjamin called it a win-win and agreed to explore it further.
- Encouraged by our rapport and mutual benefits, I felt optimistic about proposing a joint venture. I told Benjamin we were ready for the next level. Benjamin agreed and asked what I had in mind. I proposed co-developing a platform integrating risk management with financial planning for entrepreneurs. Benjamin called it groundbreaking and said combining our expertise could set us apart. I said we could leverage our strengths. Benjamin suggested drafting initial plans.

I do not have access to Benjamin’s private thoughts, internal motives, exact education level beyond “limited formal education,” MBTI type, or any events or dialogue I did not personally observe or participate in.
